children: The NHAI project covers the Karvad-Jujuwa section, with construction scheduled for completion within 18 months under the EPC model

Infrastructure company Ashoka Buildcon has emerged as the lowest bidder (L1) for a Rs 865.90-crore contract awarded by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) for the Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway in Gujarat.

The project involves completing the remaining construction work on an eight-lane, access-controlled stretch between Km 128.0 and Km 154.6, covering the Karvad-Jujuwa section in Gujarat, the company said in a regulatory filing dated 5 November.

The contract will be executed under the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) mode, with a quoted value of Rs 865.90 crore, excluding goods and services tax (GST). Ashoka Buildcon has been given 18 months to complete the work. The project also carries a defect liability period of 10 years, according to the regulatory filing. The contract covers the balance construction work on the specified section of the expressway.

The latest order follows a Rs 290.23-crore contract secured by Ashoka Buildcon from North Eastern Railway last month. The contract involves upgrading electric traction power supply installations in Uttar Pradesh.

The project covers the Gorakhpur Cantt-Chhapra Gramin section of the Varanasi division. Its scope includes the design, supply, erection, testing and commissioning of traction substations and associated switching posts for a 2x25 kV AC traction feeding system.
The railway contract will also be executed under the EPC mode, with a completion timeline of 24 months from the commencement date. It carries a defect liability period of two years.
